item.title: The Day I Became a Woman: Three Women, One Journey
item.description:
What does freedom mean?

Does it mean being allowed to play outside? Being allowed to ride a bicycle? Being allowed to spend your own money? The Day I Became a Woman explores these questions through three stories about women at different ages…….

It was a windy day and Hava’s mom is waking Hava up from her bed inside of a small white - cloth tent. Hava is a small, energetic girl with black, wavy hair up to her shoulders with short bangs. She is wearing sandals and a frock that hangs up to her knees. She lives with her grandmother and mother. They are a Muslim family living in Iran, and in her tradition, a girl becomes a woman on her ninth birthday. Once Hava gets out of bed, she is informed by her grandmother that it is her birthday. Therefore, Hava has now become a woman. She must wear a Chador and she cannot talk or play with boys. Hava’s grandmother and mother immediately start sewing Hava a Chador to wear.
